fullSource:
use IO.Std.write_line

class ANIMAL is
    init() is si

    speak() -> string => "an animal"
si

class DOG: ANIMAL is
    _barks: int

    init() is
        super.init()
        _barks = 0
    si

    bark() -> DOG is
        _barks = _barks + 1
        return self
    si

    speak() -> string => "{super.speak()} that barked {_barks} times"
si

let factorial = n rec => if n == 0 then 1 else n * rec(n - 1) fi

let missing: string? = null

let (_, second) = (1, "two")

write_line("self      {DOG().bark().bark().speak()}")
write_line("super     {DOG().speak()}")
write_line("null      an absent value tests as {missing?}")
write_line("true      {1 == 1} and false {1 == 2}")
write_line("_         discards a value: {second}")
write_line("_[T]      the default value of an int: {_[int]}")
write_line("rec       a function literal calls itself: {factorial(5)}")
output:
self      an animal that barked 2 times
super     an animal that barked 0 times
null      an absent value tests as False
true      True and false False
_         discards a value: two
_[T]      the default value of an int: 0
rec       a function literal calls itself: 120
